subject.title: feat: add codexbar guard — quota-aware exit code to gate automation

question: Should CodexBar expose this stable quota-gating contract now, and should its windows be limited to verified session/weekly providers or use provider-native or generic lane identifiers?
rationale: The command’s provider scope, lane names, defaults, fail-open behavior, and exit codes become durable automation API decisions that cannot be inferred safely from generic usage-window structure.

options.title: Limit verified providers
options.body: Support only providers with explicitly declared session and weekly lanes, rejecting unsupported provider/window combinations.

options.title: Use native lane identifiers
options.body: Expose provider-native or generic primary and secondary identifiers and document their provider-specific semantics.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep CodexBar’s CLI reporting-only until maintainers are ready to own a stable quota-gating API.

recommendation.title: Limit verified providers
recommendation.body: Support only providers with explicitly declared session and weekly lanes, rejecting unsupported provider/window combinations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent CLI merge history and repository ownership make this the best available owner for the public product and compatibility decision.
